body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT. I checked #2029's current state rather than repeating my 13:29 reading,
since you have now made it the critical path for two specs.

STILL BLOCKED, and worse than when I last looked:

    #2029  OPEN  CONFLICTING/DIRTY  head db449a262e  last updated 20:28:07Z
    behind main by 3 commits

The conflict is a content conflict in aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs. Two files overlap with main:
lib.rs and tests/task_1265_rework_no_op_tests.rs — the second auto-merges; only lib.rs conflicts.

WHAT CREATED IT, because it bears on ordering. All three commits it is behind touch lib.rs:

    a8c1877576  BUG-1445 detect rebase-only rework rounds        (#2028)
    b09197ab72  BUG-1447 classify branch policy refusal as hold  (#2031)
    4fd51c96a9  BUG-1432 report stranded forge lookup failures   (#2024)

Two of those are drain-orchestration changes in the same region #2029 is editing, and BUG-1445
is *itself* about detecting no-op rework rounds — the same subject as BUG-1476. So this is not
incidental drift: the branch is stale against work that overlaps its own topic, and every hour
it sits the overlap grows, because that region of lib.rs is where tonight's drain fixes land.

THE ORDERING ARGUMENT IS NOW STRONGER THAN "resolve it ahead of work with no blocked dependents".
The longer #2029 waits, the more expensive its own rebase becomes, and it is the generator for
BUG-1495's noise while it waits. Cost of delay is compounding rather than flat.

I am NOT touching it — resolving a content conflict is implementation and it is not my seat.
Flagging it as a read, with the file and the three commits named, so whoever picks it up starts
from the conflict rather than from discovery.

ONE THING I WOULD NOT ASSUME: I have not looked at whether the lib.rs conflict is mechanical
(adjacent edits) or semantic (both sides changing the same guard). BUG-1445 detecting no-op
rework rounds and BUG-1476 arming a no-change guard from PR verdicts could easily be two
implementations of overlapping intent, in which case the rebase is a design question rather than
a merge. Worth someone establishing which before it is handed to an implementer as a rebase
task — that is the difference between a ten-minute job and a round.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
